standard_prerequisites.name: The description of the total ring of fractions of a ring all of whose weakly associated primes are minimal, and the identification of nonzerodivisors with elements outside the weakly associated primes
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Cited at proof lines 6102-6106 and again at 6126-6129
standard_prerequisites.use: Gives the product decomposition of the total ring of fractions over affine opens and the statement about nonzerodivisors.

standard_prerequisites.name: The compatibility of the sheaf of meromorphic functions with tensor products by quasi-coherent modules, and the identification of rational functions with meromorphic functions on an integral scheme
standard_prerequisites.use: Derives the statement about meromorphic sections of an arbitrary quasi-coherent module from the main identity, and handles part of the comparison with rational functions.

standard_prerequisites.name: Pullbacks of meromorphic functions along a morphism whose fibres are integral, cited from the same chapter, together with quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness of the coproduct morphism and quasi-coherence of its pushforward of the structure sheaf
standard_prerequisites.use: Produces the comparison map from the sheaf of meromorphic functions to the pushforward and gives its quasi-coherence.

core_obligations: Preliminary reductions: a locally finite direct sum of sheaves equals the product, and since meromorphic sections of a quasi-coherent module are obtained by tensoring it with the sheaf of meromorphic functions, the statement about meromorphic sections follows from the main identity; the comparison with rational functions is reduced to the case of finitely many generic points and extended by glueing (proof lines 6075-6083).

Reduce to one identity: forming the coproduct of the canonical morphisms from the spectra of the local rings at the generic points, the task is to show that the sheaf of meromorphic functions is the pushforward of the structure sheaf along it; on the coproduct the sheaf of meromorphic functions equals the structure sheaf because a nonzerodivisor in a local ring of dimension zero is a unit (proof lines 6085-6092).

Compare on affine opens: pullbacks of meromorphic functions along the coproduct morphism are defined, which yields a map from the sheaf of meromorphic functions to that pushforward; on an affine open the coordinate ring has finitely many minimal primes, every weakly associated prime is one of them, and the total ring of fractions is the product of the localizations at those primes, so the value of the naive presheaf already agrees with the pushforward, and the map is an isomorphism (proof lines 6094-6112).

Conclude the listed properties: the structure sheaf of the coproduct is quasi-coherent as a pushforward because the coproduct morphism is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, which gives the quasi-coherence claim; the statement about nonzerodivisors follows from choosing around a point an affine open all of whose components pass through it and using that elements outside the maximal-prime set are nonzerodivisors, and the statement about stalks follows by computing stalks (proof lines 6114-6132).
proof_roadmap: Reduce the quasi-coherent-module and rational-function statements to the single identity for the sheaf of meromorphic functions, and rewrite that identity as a pushforward along the coproduct of the local rings at the generic points (proof lines 6075-6092).

Verify the identity on affine opens through the product decomposition of the total ring of fractions, then read off quasi-coherence, the nonzerodivisor statement and the stalk statement (proof lines 6094-6132).
difficulty_reason: The lemma says that for a scheme whose weakly associated points are generic points of components and whose components are locally finite, the sheaf of meromorphic functions is simultaneously the direct sum and the product of the skyscrapers at the generic points, with consequences for meromorphic sections of quasi-coherent modules, the description of nonzerodivisors, the total quotient rings of local rings and of affine coordinate rings, and the identification of rational with meromorphic functions (statement lines 6034-6073). The counted proof has two layers: it reduces everything to the identity for the sheaf of meromorphic functions, rewritten as a pushforward along the coproduct morphism from the local rings at the generic points, and it verifies that identity on affine opens using the product decomposition of the total ring of fractions, from which quasi-coherence, the nonzerodivisor statement and the stalk statement follow (proof lines 6075-6132). It is H2: the reductions and the affine computation are carried out in the counted span, with the cited inputs being the total ring of fractions and pullback statements.
